items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: and I believe the first time Bill Evans was working with the band.

ctx.x: I got acquainted with those guys and I told them how many weeks I wanted them and we (inaudible). That's where I first got a hold of Wallace Wilks, the trumpet player, and I believe the first time Bill Evans was working with the band.

items.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Um I stayed with him about a year, maybe all of ’46. And then in ’47 I, I left Ernie and went to Chicago

ctx.x: Um...but that was before any of us had heard Hootie Blues with Jay McShann and Charlie Parker, and Sonny made about-face and he seemed like more influenced by Charlie Parker. Um anyway, that band only lasted a couple of weeks, and so I returned to Detroit. And then in about ’46, Lucky Thompson recommended to the Lucky Millinder Band. So I joined them in New York in about ’46. Um, at least I, he sent for me. I went to New York, I was supposed to take the tenor player’s place who was supposed to go with Cab…
